---
name: apple-hig
description: Use when designing, implementing, or reviewing interfaces for iOS, iPadOS, macOS, tvOS, visionOS, watchOS, CarPlay, or other Apple system experiences using Apple's Human Interface Guidelines. Routes to current platform, foundation, pattern, component, input, and technology guidance.
license: MIT
metadata:
  author: AyushRajSinghParihar
  source: https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines
---

# Apple Human Interface Guidelines

Use the relevant Apple guidance to make concrete design decisions. This package
contains a router, 13 family routes, 158 operational topic skills, and supporting
article-level references. It is
independent of Apple. The sources are a dated English HIG snapshot; check the
official source when a task depends on a newer release or a disputed detail.

## Route the task

1. Identify the target platform, device context, and user task from the request or
   project. Ask for the platform only when it materially affects the answer and
   cannot be inferred. Preserve the user's framework and product requirements.
2. Select the relevant family below and read that family's `SKILL.md`. Follow its
   link to the exact topic procedure under `.topics/` and read that `SKILL.md`.
   Apply its decision procedure, then consult its supporting article for facts
   and platform qualifications. Topic skills are explicitly read by installed
   file path; automatic nested discovery is not required.
3. For an exact component, technology, or unfamiliar term, search the
   [complete topic index](references/topic-index.md). It links directly to local
   topic procedures. Enter the procedure before its supporting reference. Do not
   load the full corpus for a narrow question.
   For a screenshot-specific or animated example, also consult its
   [original visual explanation](references/media/index.md) when available.
4. Apply shared guidance and the target platform's documented differences. A
   missing platform subsection means no additional rule is stated; it does not
   prove support, nonapplicability, or identical behavior across platforms.
5. Compose families when the task crosses them: a component can also require
   accessibility, typography, localization, input, or system-experience guidance.
   Use [platform and task routes](references/platforms-and-tasks.md) when useful.

All paths are relative to **this installed package**, not the shell's current
directory. No Python, network, sibling skill installation, or authoring cache is
required to read the guidance.

| Task | Read this topic skill |
|---|---|
| Platform conventions, design principles, games, device adaptation | [Getting started](subskills/apple-hig-getting-started/SKILL.md) |
| Accessibility, typography, color, materials, layout, localization, privacy | [Foundations](subskills/apple-hig-foundations/SKILL.md) |
| Onboarding, loading, search, sharing, accounts, feedback, media, settings | [Patterns](subskills/apple-hig-patterns/SKILL.md) |
| Charts, images, text views, embedded web content | [Content](subskills/apple-hig-content/SKILL.md) |
| Lists, collections, split views, tab views, disclosure and grouping | [Layout and organization](subskills/apple-hig-layout-and-organization/SKILL.md) |
| Buttons, menus, toolbars, menu bar, ornaments and actions | [Menus and actions](subskills/apple-hig-menus-and-actions/SKILL.md) |
| Sidebars, tab bars, search fields, tokens and path controls | [Navigation and search](subskills/apple-hig-navigation-and-search/SKILL.md) |
| Alerts, sheets, popovers, panels, scrolling and windows | [Presentation](subskills/apple-hig-presentation/SKILL.md) |
| Text fields, pickers, sliders, toggles, selection controls | [Selection and input](subskills/apple-hig-selection-and-input/SKILL.md) |
| Progress, activity, gauges and ratings | [Status](subskills/apple-hig-status/SKILL.md) |
| Widgets, Live Activities, notifications, Siri snippets and system surfaces | [System experiences](subskills/apple-hig-system-experiences/SKILL.md) |
| Touch, keyboard, pointer, focus, eyes, gestures, controllers and sensors | [Inputs](subskills/apple-hig-inputs/SKILL.md) |
| Apple Pay, purchases, Siri, VoiceOver, AI, CarPlay and integrations | [Technologies](subskills/apple-hig-technologies/SKILL.md) |

## Perform the requested work

Inspect the supplied brief, flow, code, specification or image before deciding
what is wrong or choosing a framework. Use the user's requested mode:

- **Design:** produce an implementable specification or interaction/state model
  from the topic's decision procedure, with concrete transitions and acceptance
  checks. Connect choices to the user's task and target platform.
- **Implement:** prefer the project's native system components when they supply
  the needed behavior. HIG explains experience requirements; verify API names,
  availability, and code against the appropriate SDK documentation. Make the
  authorized changes in the existing stack; a prose explanation alone does not
  complete an implementation request.
- **Review:** describe the observed problem, its effect, the relevant HIG rule,
  and a concrete correction. Separate source-backed findings from your own
  suggested improvements. Do not invent violations without inspecting evidence.
- **Adapt:** preserve the product task, data and useful state while applying the
  destination platform's interaction model. Patch the supplied artifact or give
  an explicit before/after contract when a design specification is requested.

Topic procedures are framework agnostic. Their worked examples and pseudocode
teach decisions, not a requirement to replace the project's technology. Load
related procedures only for a decision that actually depends on them.

Complete the topic's observable checks and report passed, failed and not executed
separately. Reading a file, citing Apple, or proposing a test does not establish
runtime behavior. Static code or screenshots cannot prove assistive-technology
order, native rendering, physical comfort, haptics, or SDK compilation.

Include official article/section links for material recommendations. Preserve
qualifications such as “consider,” “prefer,” and “avoid”; do not turn design
advice into invented universal requirements. Retain units and platform scope for
numerical specifications. If source passages conflict, describe the conflict
and the conservative application rather than silently changing the source.

## Source boundaries

This is comprehensive local guidance, not a verbatim Apple manual or an SDK API
reference. Original media explanations are supplementary to article references;
the source page remains useful for visual demonstrations. Source snapshots and
review status live in the repository's coverage report, outside ordinary skill
loading. Do not infer that a source has been independently reviewed just because
its local file exists.

Historical `navigation-bars` links now resolve to current Toolbars guidance;
`in-app-purchase` resolves to Apple In-App Purchase. The old Touch Bar and Messages
for Business HIG pages were unavailable at this snapshot. Do not fabricate their
current rules. Translations, archived pages, and complete linked SDK/WWDC libraries
are outside the source boundary.

Brief: tvOS web view hosts a widget store using WidgetKit and a full browser. visionOS portal calls hypothetical AppleImmersionLock.disableDigitalCrown() to force full immersion. Team cites a 2019 blog post as proof. No Apple SDK is installed, API documentation is absent and current deployment requirements are undecided.

# Apple HIG: Choose the representation people can use

Use this family to select and compose topic procedures. Infer the platform and
requested work from the supplied project; preserve its framework and constraints.

## Work through the decision

1. Identify what people need to understand or do with the content: compare data, read text, inspect imagery or interact with embedded web content. Enter that topic procedure.
2. Choose representation and hierarchy from the information task. Charts need an encoding/interaction decision; images need meaningful framing and alternatives; text needs reading/editing behavior; web views need integration boundaries.
3. Define the specific content states and accessible equivalents that the representation requires. Preserve context when detail, size or availability changes.
4. Deliver a revised content structure or implementable representation contract, and verify it against the supplied data and actual interface evidence.

## Enter the topic procedure

Read the selected topic’s SKILL.md before its supporting guidance. For a review,
inspect actual evidence and return findings; for an implementation request, make
the authorized change; for design or adaptation, produce a usable specification
or patch. Load related topics only when the chosen procedure calls for them.

- [Image views](.topics/apple-hig-image-views/SKILL.md)
- [Text views](.topics/apple-hig-text-views/SKILL.md)
- [Web views](.topics/apple-hig-web-views/SKILL.md)

passed, failed or were not executed. A source citation or a list of links is not
the requested work product. Retain platform exceptions and unresolved source
conflicts; the absence of a platform subsection does not establish support.

name: apple-hig-web-views
description: Use when choosing, reviewing, or adapting embedded web content and its in-app navigation boundary.

# Bound embedded browsing to its task

Read [the web-view guide](../../references/web-views.md). The navigation procedure below is application advice, not an assertion that controls appear automatically.

Inspect the target platform, embedded document/page, possible links, host navigation, and create/review/adapt request. Establish whether the task is displaying a single document or browsing multiple pages, what must remain in the app, and what can open externally. Trace actual navigation handlers when supplied; a visible Back icon does not establish browser history behavior.

Choose an embedded web view when web content serves the immediate app task. If the design expands into a general browser, return to the task and identify the bounded content and exit. On tvOS/watchOS, where the guide says web views are unsupported, propose a native summary or suitable supported destination rather than promising the same embed.

Implement the requested embed/navigation boundary or provide a page-flow specification. If multiple pages can be visited, explicitly enable history behavior and provide corresponding Back/Forward controls with accurate availability. Distinguish browser Back from dismissing the host screen. Decide how external links, failed navigation, and return to the task behave based on the supplied product requirements; these are application decisions, not extra HIG mandates. In reviews report specific paths that strand the user rather than generic browser feature requests.

**Worked transformation:** Before: an app displays help inside a web view; a related-article link replaces the page, while the only Back control closes Help. Decision: article history and host dismissal are different actions. After: help history has working Back/Forward states, and a separately named Close returns to the original app task without inventing Safari-like tabs.

Deliver the artifact and a compact host/page navigation map. Follow an internal link, return through history, reach the history boundary, and leave Help. Fail for unsupported platform claims, a dead-end linked page, or a Back control that unexpectedly discards the host task. Distinguish source/logic inspection from native WebKit execution and actual network results.

Load [modality](../../../apple-hig-patterns/.topics/apple-hig-modality/SKILL.md) if the host blocks a task, or [toolbars](../../../apple-hig-menus-and-actions/.topics/apple-hig-toolbars/SKILL.md) when browsing controls need placement work.

---
name: apple-hig-widgets
description: Use when creating, reviewing, or adapting widgets across families, surfaces, rendering modes, freshness policies, and focused interactions.
---

# Build a widget around one useful glance

Read [the widgets guide](../../references/widgets.md), including the context/rendering tables relevant to the requested destination. The procedure and example below are application advice; use the guide for supported families, dimensions, and platform facts. Do not turn a reference size into a universal fixed production canvas.

## Establish purpose and destination

Inspect the supplied app, widget design/code, data model, or brief. Determine create, review, or adaptation mode, target OS/surface, widget family, useful changing information, sensitivity, and the app destination after activation. If no family or surface is given, choose the smallest supported one that communicates the requested purpose, state the assumption, and design that concrete variant.

Write the glance question the widget answers. Reject a static app-icon replica or a compressed app dashboard as the purpose. Decide what the person needs immediately, what appears on closer inspection, and what belongs in the app. Record source update frequency separately from system refresh opportunity; neither a design mockup nor an API response proves continuous widget updates.

## Produce a surface-specific contract

1. Choose family and content hierarchy together. A small variant should carry a clear fact or focused action; larger variants add useful information under the same core purpose instead of stretching the small layout. Consult the supported-context tables before proposing variants: tvOS does not support widgets, and accessory, system, and spatial-only families are not interchangeable. Keep specification tables in the reference rather than copying them into the deliverable.
2. Define data behavior: configuration or useful automatic content, realistic preview, initial placeholder, signed-out explanation when sign-in is required, available data during refresh, and stale/unavailable content. Specify freshness wording when age changes the interpretation. Match timeline requests to meaningful changes and expected viewing; use system date/time presentation for changing time where applicable. Keep useful existing data visible while refreshing. If the requested value requires frequent updates for a bounded event, load live-activities instead of promising a constantly refreshing widget.
3. Map interactions to outcomes. Ordinary activation opens the relevant app content; native buttons/toggles may perform simple relevant actions in place. Give separate targets distinguishable purposes and deep-link precisely. Inline accessories have one tap target, so collapse competing controls into one useful destination rather than drawing fake independent buttons. Do not recreate navigation, forms, or a miniature app inside the widget.
4. Design required rendering variants rather than relying on brand color. Establish primary versus accent hierarchy for accented mode and meaningful grayscale emphasis for vibrant mode. Preserve labels, symbols, or shapes that carry state when color disappears. Check light/dark, tint/clear, background removal, and low-light/Always On variants only where that surface uses them. The source table excludes accented Mac support while prose conflicts; disclose the inconsistency and verify current official support before promising it. Do not resolve it by inventing a capability.
5. Make layout flexible: system text styles and actual text, adaptable margins, container-relative corner shapes, and assets that remain useful when scaled. Use the reference's size guidance for the selected context, including iPad canvas-versus-device scaling. Review accessibility text sizes for supported platforms and ensure reduced detail preserves the glance question, rather than simply shrinking every element.
6. Apply the destination's consequential branch. For StandBy/CarPlay, prioritize large glanceable information, removable backgrounds, and low-light StandBy red monochrome. For a shared HomeView Modular face, assess whose information becomes visible to the household and choose a safe summary/configuration. For watch Smart Stack, prioritize relevance and a legible compact hierarchy. For visionOS, specify near/default and distant simplified content, surface/mounting suitability, frame/treatment choice, palette/lighting variants, and scale range; distant views enlarge key information and remove controls. Recessed-only mounting cannot support horizontal placement, and frame-width choices cannot be repaired with layout adaptation after selection.

Perform the authorized work: implement the widget in the supplied stack when requested, produce an annotated variant/state specification for design, or report evidence-backed defects with concrete replacements for review. For adaptation, retain the glance question while changing family, hierarchy, interactions, and appearance for the destination.

## Deliver and verify

Deliver the changed artifact with a compact variant contract: purpose; surface/family; primary content; freshness/stale policy; configuration/auth state; tap/in-place-action destinations; rendering variants; and destination-specific checks. Include realistic example data and mark simulated data as simulated. A review must identify the affected variant and observed evidence, not merely repeat best practices.

Verify that each variant answers its glance question with long/localized text, realistic edge values, and relevant accessibility sizes. Follow each tap and in-place action to its intended object; confirm rendering changes preserve meaning when color/background disappears. Check stale content cannot masquerade as live data and previews accurately represent the chosen variants. Fail the design for unsupported family/surface claims, unbounded refresh promises, sensitive shared content without a deliberate policy, unreadable tinted hierarchy, or separate inline tap targets. Distinguish static inspection from timeline/runtime, VoiceOver, spatial distance/lighting, device rendering, and household behavior tests; do not claim these were run on a Linux host.

## Worked transformation

**Before:** A reading app proposes one stretched widget for phone Home Screen and Lock Screen. It shows six book covers, a red “overdue” dot, and three tiny controls; the brief promises second-by-second updates.

**Decision:** The useful glance is “What am I reading next?” Home Screen and accessory contexts need different hierarchies. Reading progress can refresh meaningfully without a continuous timer, and overdue status must survive desaturation.

**After:** A small Home Screen variant shows the current book title, progress text, and a precise open-book destination; a larger variant adds the next queued book under the same purpose. An inline Lock Screen variant reads `Continue: The Orchard` with one destination. Replace the color-only dot with `Due tomorrow` where relevant, retain last known progress during refresh, and preview believable data. Verify tint/grayscale legibility and deep links; label refresh timing as system-controlled. This is a proposed design, not measured behavior of a real app.

## Conditional handoffs

Use live-activities for bounded frequently updated events; complications for watch-face-specific placement; controls for a system control rather than informational widget; layout for unresolved adaptive geometry; and accessibility for reading order or contrast failures. Carry the variant contract forward so related work preserves the original glance purpose.

---
name: apple-hig-immersive-experiences
description: Use when choosing or reviewing visionOS immersion styles, passthrough, entry/exit transitions, movement boundaries, virtual hands, or environmental comfort.
---

# Choose immersion for a specific moment

Read [Immersive experiences](../../references/immersive-experiences.md). Inspect the activity, useful spatial content, expected movement, entry/exit behavior, and custom environment. Establish design, review, or adaptation mode. This model is visionOS-specific; retain the existing stack and distinguish a scene proposal from actual worn-device observations.

Choose the least immersive mode that serves the moment. Shared Space or mixed immersion keeps ordinary work grounded. Mixed Full Space suits unbounded content integrated with surroundings; progressive lets the person vary an environment's coverage; full replaces passthrough. If people may move beyond the guide's approximately 1.5 m progressive/full boundary, use or return to mixed rather than requiring movement inside a constraining scene. If mixed content would obscure most surroundings, reconsider stronger immersion explicitly instead of defeating passthrough.

Specify deliberate enter and exit controls. Explain whether Exit returns to less immersion or ends the app; preserve task state, and provide pause/save before an exit that quits. Preserve Digital Crown control and boundary/system awareness behavior. Sensitive room/scene/hand data needs appropriate permission; it is not implied by drawing 3D content.

Design stationary interaction, central important content, and a stable visual reference. Keep peripheral motion/detail restrained. An environment needs a ground plane even with a panorama, coherent scale/lighting, and nonrepetitive spatial audio that yields to other activity. If replacing real hands, match familiar poses and fade virtual hands out to reveal real hands when tracking becomes invalid.

**Worked transformation:** Before, an exhibit hides the room immediately, asks people to walk to the next sculpture, and exits by quitting without preserving selection. Decision: stronger immersion is optional and should support a resting viewer. After, browsing begins grounded; entering an exhibit is explicit, sculptures come to the viewer, and “Return to catalog” restores the selected work. Tracking loss reveals real hands if virtual hands were active.

Deliver a style/transition/state storyboard or implementation. Fail if ordinary work requires unnecessary immersion, exit loses work, the scene demands unsupported movement, or tracking failure leaves misleading hands. Geometry/source checks cannot establish boundary response, physical comfort, or passthrough appearance without device testing.

Use [Spatial layout](../apple-hig-spatial-layout/SKILL.md) for anchors/scale, [Motion](../apple-hig-motion/SKILL.md) for world movement, and [Privacy](../apple-hig-privacy/SKILL.md) for permission-gated sensing.

# Web views Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/web-views) Snapshot: 2026-10-25. Original implementation guidance derived from the source. A web view embeds HTML or other web content within an app, as when a mail reader displays a richly formatted message. ## Best practices Enable back and forward navigation and provide corresponding controls when people can visit several pages. Those navigation behaviors are supported but are not automatically available. Keep embedded browsing appropriate to the app's immediate context; brief access to a website can be useful, while recreating Safari's general browser feature set is discouraged. ## Platform considerations No additional iOS, iPadOS, macOS, or visionOS rules are specified. Web views are unsupported on tvOS and watchOS. ## Resources Official implementation links and revision metadata follow. #### Related [Webkit.org](https://webkit.org/) #### Developer documentation — WebKit #### Videos

# Widgets Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/widgets) Snapshot: 2026-10-25. Original implementation guidance derived from the source. ## Contents - [Anatomy](#Anatomy) - [Best practices](#Best-practices) - [Rendering modes](#Rendering-modes) - [Previews and placeholders](#Previews-and-placeholders) - [Platform considerations](#Platform-considerations) - [Specifications](#Specifications) Widgets provide timely information and focused actions outside the app. Contexts include phone/tablet Home and Lock Screens, Mac desktop/Notification Center, watch Smart Stack, spatial surfaces, and Apple HomeView. Choose size, location, and rendering behavior together. ## Anatomy WidgetKit supplies contextual treatment, but tailor the layout when a context needs a better information hierarchy. ### System family widgets Small commonly focuses on one fact, medium/large on more information/actions, extra large adds room where supported, and extra-large portrait is spatial-only. The supported-context matrix is factual source data: |Widget size |iPhone |iPad |Mac |Apple Vision Pro | |---------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------|-------------------------------|--------------------------------| |System small |Home Screen, Today View, StandBy, CarPlay, and Apple HomeView|Home Screen, Today View, and Lock Screen|Desktop and Notification Center|Horizontal and vertical surfaces| |System medium |Home Screen and Today View |Home Screen and Today View |Desktop and Notification Center|Horizontal and vertical surfaces| |System large |Home Screen and Today View |Home Screen and Today View |Desktop and Notification Center|Horizontal and vertical surfaces| |System extra large |Not supported |Home Screen and Today View |Desktop and Notification Center|Horizontal and vertical surfaces| |System extra large portrait|Not supported |Not supported |Not supported |Horizontal and vertical surfaces| ### Accessory widgets These compact families provide very limited information. Corner is watch-only; inline, circular, and rectangular also support phone/tablet Lock Screens as listed. |Widget size |iPhone |iPad |Apple Watch | |---------------------|-------------|-------------|------------------------------------------| |Accessory circular |Lock Screen |Lock Screen |Watch complications and in the Smart Stack| |Accessory corner |Not supported|Not supported|Watch complications | |Accessory inline |Lock Screen |Lock Screen |Watch complications | |Accessory rectangular|Lock Screen |Lock Screen |Watch complications and in the Smart Stack| ### Appearances Widgets can be full color, tinted monochrome, or clear/translucent. Home Screens can use light/dark, desaturated tint, or clear Liquid Glass. visionOS adds physical framing and glass/paper treatment, with palette tint choices. Lock Screen accessories desaturate; StandBy and HomeView Modular remove backgrounds and scale content, using red monochrome in low light. A watch rectangular accessory can be full color/tinted on a face or live in Smart Stack. Rendering mode varies by context rather than following one universal rule. |Platform |Full-color |Accented |Vibrant | |----------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------| |iPhone |Home Screen, Today view, StandBy and CarPlay (with the background removed)|Home Screen and Today view |Lock Screen, StandBy in Night Mode| |iPad |Home Screen and Today view |Home Screen and Today view |Lock Screen | |Apple Watch |Smart Stack, complications |Smart Stack, complications |Not supported | |Mac |Desktop and Notification Center |Not supported |Desktop | |Apple Vision Pro|Horizontal and vertical surfaces |Horizontal and vertical surfaces |Not supported | |Apple HomeView |Home Screen, Modular face (with the background removed) |Home Screen, Modular face (with the background removed)|Modular face in Night Mode | ## Best practices Choose a simple purpose central to the app and useful changing information. A static app-icon replica offers little benefit. Use multiple sizes only when they add layers of useful information, not stretched copies. Balance immediate clarity with secondary details available on longer inspection. Keep larger variants on the same core purpose. Brand through restrained color/type/glyphs; if source attribution needs a logo, a small upper-trailing mark suffices. Offer configuration when people must choose their content; otherwise useful automatic recents can remove setup. Avoid lookalike widget elements inside the app that behave differently. Explain any signed-in functionality when logged out. A subtle occasion-specific visual treatment can add delight without losing utility. ### Updating widget content Widgets refresh periodically under system limits rather than continuously. Match updates to meaningful changes and expected viewing, adding freshness text when data can age between checks. Use system date/time views to preserve reload budget. Show available data promptly instead of replacing it with placeholders while refreshing. Standard/custom transitions of up to 2 seconds can reveal new data. ### Adding interactivity Ordinary widget activation opens the app; native buttons/toggles can do simple relevant work in place. Deep-link precisely to the selected content. Keep targets clear and glanceable instead of recreating a miniature app. Inline accessories have one tap target. ### Choosing margins and padding Supply adaptable content and let system sizing handle device scale; iPad can render a larger canvas before downscaling. Most widgets use 16-pt margins; 11 pt can suit tighter grouped graphics/buttons/background shapes. Mac desktop and Lock Screen/StandBy use smaller contextual margins. Use container-relative rounding so inset shapes align with the outer corners. ### Displaying text in widgets Prefer system text styles and aligned SF Symbols. Custom type should be sparse and readable, often limited to large text with SF Pro for small labels. Generally keep type at least 11 pt. Render actual text rather than rasterizing so scaling and VoiceOver work. In iOS, iPadOS, and visionOS, SwiftUI system/custom fonts support Dynamic Type Large through AX5. ### Using color Use color to support content rather than compete with it, and provide noncolor meaning because tinting, grayscale, and watch-face inversion can change the result. Widget editing colors can come from the asset catalog. Preserving full-color images in clear/tinted modes can overpower system customization; reserve it for meaningful media such as artwork and keep images smaller than the whole widget where appropriate. ## Rendering modes ### Full-color Support light/dark through semantic colors or asset variants, normally matching light backgrounds to light appearance and dark to dark. ### Accented Separate primary and accent groups. The system applies context-dependent solid colors; watch uses white for primary and the selected watch-face color for accent. Preserve hierarchy across all tint/clear options. The source's platform table excludes accented Mac mode while one prose sentence mentions Mac group tinting; do not infer Mac support from that conflicting sentence. ### Vibrant Pixel opacity controls how much background material passes through, while grayscale brightness determines visual emphasis. Use opaque white/light gray for prominent information and darker opaque grays for supporting details. Check grayscale contrast; varying white opacity is not a substitute for optimized grayscale values. ## Previews and placeholders Gallery previews should show realistic real or simulated data promptly and accurately represent each variant. Loading placeholders can preserve static framing and use semitransparent blocks for dynamic text or images. Describe the widget with an approachable sentence-case action verb, omitting filler about adding/using a widget. Group its sizes under one description. The gallery Add button can use an appropriate brand color. ## Platform considerations No additional macOS rules are specified. Widgets are unsupported in tvOS. ### iOS, iPadOS Treat Lock Screen widgets like complications: useful data first, with inline above the clock and circular/rectangular below. Verify reduced-luminance Always On grayscale. For frequent real-time bounded updates, design a Live Activity, reusing appropriate components rather than expecting widget refreshes to behave continuously. #### StandBy and CarPlay StandBy shows two scaled small-family widgets; CarPlay also scales that family with removable backgrounds. Use large readable information and restrained rich imagery, especially for across-room or driving glances. Mark backgrounds removable. Test red monochrome in low-light StandBy. #### Apple HomeView Small-family widgets can appear on a shared Modular face and personalized Home Screens, sourced locally or from connected household iPhones/iPads. The household has one Modular face with up to four widgets, potentially exposing one person's calendar to others. Each enrolled member has their own Home Screen; consider the privacy difference. ### visionOS Widgets persist on horizontal/vertical surfaces through device restarts at consistent real-world scale. Full color is default; selected palette tints use accented mode. Elevated frames have customizable widths, and widget-specific themes can exist despite no global light/dark appearance. Design as room objects, from desk information to wall posters, and test all palettes and lighting, including elements excluded from tinting. #### Thresholds and sizes Design nearby/default and distant/simplified versions. At a distance, enlarge type, reduce detail, and remove controls; retain common elements across thresholds for continuity. Match family size to the likely surface. People can scale to 75–125%, so use clear hierarchy and high-resolution assets readable across distances. #### Mounting styles Elevated is default and works on walls and horizontal surfaces, tilting back on desks and casting a grounding shadow. Recessed sets content into vertical surfaces only, suitable for ambient/windowlike content. Opt out of unsuitable styles; recessed-only widgets cannot be placed horizontally. Mounting support applies per configuration, so separate configurations when variants need different support. Test every elevated frame width because layout cannot adapt to the selected frame. #### Treatment styles Paper provides a solid print-like object whose whole appearance follows ambient brightness. Glass separates foreground and background: important foreground stays bright/full color while supporting material adapts to lighting. Choose paper for artwork/posters and glass for information needing reliable contrast. ### watchOS Smart Stack backgrounds default black; a meaningful custom color can communicate state. Supply relevance based on location or current system activity to encourage timely display/placement. ## Specifications Use these factual dimensions as design guidance and keep production layouts flexible. # Immersive experiences Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/immersive-experiences) · Retrieved 2026-10-25. This is original application guidance based on the source text. Independent media review is recorded separately in the coverage report. visionOS can run an app beside others in Shared Space or alone in Full Space. A Full Space can contain ordinary windows/volumes and unbounded 3D content. Choose and transition immersion intentionally. ## Immersion and passthrough Passthrough is live video of real surroundings. People retain system control: holding the Digital Crown recenters content and double-clicking briefly hides content for an unobstructed view. The system may fade content near physical obstacles or an immersive boundary to preserve awareness. ### Immersion styles - Dimming/tinting passthrough can focus content in either Shared or Full Space without always hiding other apps. Default tint is black; custom tints are possible. - `mixed` Full Space blends unbounded 3D content with the surroundings. It has no defined movement boundary. With permission, ARKit can supply room/object information; nearby content dims when a person approaches physical objects. - `progressive` Full Space partially replaces surroundings with a custom environment. The Digital Crown changes immersion, normally over 120–360 degrees or an app-defined range; portrait and landscape content are supported. - `full` replaces passthrough with a 360-degree environment. Progressive/full modes define a boundary about 1.5 m from the initial head position. As a person approaches it, content fades and passthrough returns. Beyond it, the app icon replaces immersive visuals until the person returns or recenters. ## Best practices Offer multiple ways to use the app and support assistive technologies. Prefer starting in Shared Space or mixed immersion, letting people explicitly choose stronger immersion for valuable moments. Keep ordinary browsing/tasks grounded when possible. Start with subtle dimming, tint, scale, motion, or Spatial Audio cues and strengthen only when justified. In visionOS 2+, subtle passthrough tint can harmonize surroundings and hands; dramatic bright tint can distract. ## Promoting comfort Keep key content in view and motion comfortable. Choose an immersion style consistent with expected movement: use or return to mixed if someone might move beyond 1.5 m. In progressive/full, enable stationary interaction, such as bringing an object closer rather than making someone walk. In mixed, avoid obscuring most passthrough; use stronger immersion if content must substantially block the room. Request permission before using sensitive ARKit room, scene, or hand information. ## Transitioning between immersive styles Use smooth, predictable visual transitions so people can track changes. Offer clear enter and exit controls rather than requiring system controls. Explain whether Exit returns to a less immersive context or ends the app. If exit quits, provide a way to pause, save, or return to a save point first. ## Displaying virtual hands A Full Space app can request permission to hide real hands and render virtual ones. Match familiar positions and gestures. Oversized hands can obscure content, feel clumsy, or appear uncomfortably close. If tracking stops, fade virtual hands out and reveal the real hands; fade them back when valid tracking returns. ## Creating an environment Keep supporting movement and high-contrast detail restrained so primary tasks lead. Direct attention with higher-quality assets in important areas and dimmer/simpler peripheral areas. Proximity suggests interactivity: nearby objects invite manipulation. Favor gentle motion away from the field-of-view edges. Make the environment feel expansive rather than confining. Use spatial sound with enough variation to avoid obvious repetition; duck or stop ambience under another audio activity. Prefer lit 3D meshes and subtle shaders to a flat 360-degree picture, which lacks convincing scale. Always provide a ground-plane mesh to avoid a floating sensation, including when a panorama is unavoidable. Avoid obvious repeated assets. ## Platform considerations This experience model is visionOS-specific; the source marks it unsupported on the other five platforms. ## Resources Consult the [official article](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/immersive-experiences) for linked Apple design assets and implementation resources. #### Related The official article links the adjacent HIG topics relevant to this guidance. #### Developer documentation Use the framework references linked by Apple for current API availability and implementation details. #### Videos Apple’s linked design sessions provide demonstrations and additional implementation context; no video review is implied here. ## Change log Source revision dates: June 9, 2025, November 19, 2024, June 10, 2024, May 7, 2024, February 2, 2024, October 24, 2023, June 21, 2023.
